item.title: Critical Care Management of Disaster-Related Organ Failure.
item.description: Disasters generate high volumes of multisystem trauma while simultaneously degrading the staff, equipment, and electricity that critical care depends on. This article reviews management of disaster-related organ failure under resource constraint. item.title: Resuscitation of the Trauma Patient.
item.description: This article provides a practical overview of modern trauma resuscitation for emergency clinicians. It emphasizes early recognition of shock, timely hemorrhage control, and activation of massive transfusion protocols. Guidance is provided on fluid resuscitation, permissive hypotension, airway management, and treatment of agitation in critically ill trauma patients. item.description: Prokinetic agents are used to enhance upper gastrointestinal motility, but adverse events related to these agents are poorly described. We aimed to provide detailed epidemiological data on predefined serious adverse events (SAEs) in a cohort of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with and without prokinetic treatment. item.description: Valvular heart disease is an uncommon but high-risk cause of cardiogenic shock requiring rapid, multidisciplinary management aimed at bridging patients to definitive surgical or transcatheter valve intervention. Early comprehensive Doppler echocardiography is essential, as clinical signs may be subtle. item.title: Decision making around end-of-life: Focused ethnography in two intensive care units in Vietnam.
item.description: Literature on the quality of death and dying has predominantly drawn on high-income contexts, while much less is known about end-of-life care in low-middle-income settings. In Vietnam, policy and practice around palliative and end-of-life care has not kept pace with the ageing of the population. This study explores factors influencing end-of-life decision making in intensive care units (ICUs) where formal protocols are lacking. item.description: Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. Prior studies suggest higher mortality in this population, but interpretation is limited by aggregation of heterogeneous endpoints. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock. item.description: Cardiac arrest remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, although contemporary care now enables potential survival with good neurologic outcome. The core acute management goals for survivors of cardiac arrest are to provide organ support, sustain adequate hemodynamics, and evaluate the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. A standard CRRT intensity is 20-25 mL/kg/hr, because higher doses have not improved outcomes. item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.
